review_candidates.description: Organizational Context The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian organization, with a network of 191-member National Societies (NSs). IFRC is part of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement (Movement), together with its member National Societies and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). The work of IFRC is guided by the following fundamental principles: humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality. IFRC is led by its Secretary General, and has its Headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland. The Headquarters are organized into three main Divisions: (i) National Society Development and Operations Coordination; (ii) Global Relations, Humanitarian Diplomacy and Digitalization; and (iii) Management Policy, Strategy and Corporate Services. IFRC has five regional offices in Africa, Asia Pacific, Middle East and North Africa, Europe, and the Americas. IFRC also has country cluster delegations and country delegations throughout the world. Together, the Geneva Headquarters and the field structure (regional, cluster and country) comprise the IFRC Secretariat. IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. The Federation in delivering its broader Humanitarian and Developmental mission, hosts the Country Support Platform (CSP) of the Global Task Force for Cholera Control (GTFCC) as an operational arm of the GTFCC. The International Federation of Redcross and Red Crescent -Country Support Platform (CSP) working with Zambia RedCross Society (ZRCS) and Funding from Foreign Commonwealth Development Office (FCDO), supports the implementation and institutionalization of Case Area Targeted Intervention (CATI) approach in Priority Area for Multisectoral Intervention (PAMI) districts in Zambia. This work is undertaken in collaboration with the Ministry of Health (MoH), Zambia National Public Health Institute (ZNPHI), Disaster Risk Management Division (DRMD) and other relevant partners. review_candidates.title: Junior Finance Specialist with French
review_candidates.description: Would you like to start your career in an international company and join a team that supports your development and helps you learn new things? We are looking for an attentive and responsible person who speaks English and French and enjoys working with numbers and data. No previous work experience or specialised education is required — we will teach you everything you need to know! A little about the employer: This is a global business services center providing Finance, HR, IT, and other corporate services to the company’s teams across different countries. Hundreds of professionals work here, supporting international teams, developing their skills in a multicultural environment, and building their careers within a global company. What you will do: Work with financial data and accounts: check financial information, make necessary adjustments, and reconcile data between different systems. Find and resolve discrepancies: when amounts or data do not match, identify the reason and help correct the issue. Support month-end closing: check that all transactions are recorded correctly and help the team complete financial processes at the end of each month, quarter, and year. Work with reporting: prepare and check financial data used for reporting. Communicate with colleagues in France: communicate daily in French via email and meetings to resolve financial-related questions. What we are looking for: English and French at Intermediate level or higher ; attention to detail and confidence working with numbers; basic Excel skills (formulas, pivot tables); degree in Economics or a related field (International Relations or similar fields are also welcome); willingness to learn and develop.
